A Sentinel data connector brings logs into Microsoft Sentinel, not into Insider Risk Management. Microsoft Entra Connect Sync synchronizes directory objects and does not supply HR events. A Defender for Cloud Apps app connector connects SaaS apps for visibility and control.

prompt: A works council worries that analysts reviewing Insider Risk Management alerts will immediately see employees' names and build profiles of individuals. Which built-in design feature addresses this concern?

options.text: Alerts are generated only after the affected employee consents
All alert data is encrypted with a sensitivity label
Users are pseudonymized by default, with access controls and audit logs
Alerts and their evidence are automatically deleted after 24 hours

explanation: Insider Risk Management is built with privacy by design: users are pseudonymized by default, and role-based access controls and audit logs help protect user-level privacy. Alerts do not depend on employee consent. Sensitivity labels classify and protect content rather than masking identities in alerts. Alerts are not automatically deleted after 24 hours.

prompt: An Insider Risk Management investigation shows that an employee accidentally shared a sensitive file externally and had no malicious intent. The reviewer wants to remind the employee of the policy and point them to refresher training. What should the reviewer use?

options.text: A notice from the customizable notice templates
An eDiscovery hold on the employee's mailbox

explanation: When users inadvertently violate policy conditions, Insider Risk Management reviewers can send a reminder notice from customizable notice templates, for example directing the user to refresher training. An eDiscovery hold preserves content for legal matters, which is excessive for an accidental mistake. An audit log retention policy controls how long audit records are kept. A Compliance Manager improvement action tracks regulatory control work, not individual user follow-up.

prompt: An Insider Risk Management case suggests an employee deliberately leaked trade secrets, and the legal department now needs to preserve, collect, review and export the related content as part of a formal legal process. What should the risk analyst do?

options.text: Send the user a notice and close the case
Export the alert to the Service Trust Portal
Apply a sensitivity label to the user's mailbox
Escalate the case to eDiscovery (Premium) for legal review

explanation: Insider Risk Management can escalate a case for investigation, transferring data and management to eDiscovery (Premium), which provides an end-to-end workflow to preserve, collect, review, analyze and export content and manage legal hold notifications. A notice is appropriate for inadvertent violations, not deliberate leaks. The Service Trust Portal publishes Microsoft compliance documentation and does not receive cases. Sensitivity labels apply to items and containers rather than preserving evidence.

prompt: A company has received notice of a lawsuit and must ensure that no email or OneDrive files belonging to five employees are permanently deleted, even by the employees themselves, while the case is ongoing. What should the legal team create in Microsoft Purview?

options.text: A data loss prevention policy for the five employees
An eDiscovery case with a hold on the employees' content locations
An Insider Risk Management policy for priority users
A sensitivity label with encryption for their files

explanation: An eDiscovery case can place holds on content locations such as mailboxes and OneDrive accounts, preserving electronically stored information from inadvertent or intentional deletion during an investigation. A DLP policy controls sharing of sensitive information, not deletion. An Insider Risk Management policy detects risky behavior but does not preserve content for litigation. A sensitivity label with encryption restricts who can open files but does not stop the owners deleting them.

prompt: Outside counsel asks a company for all email and Teams messages from the past year that mention a specific project code name. What is the appropriate Microsoft Purview capability for finding this content and providing it to counsel?

options.text: Activity explorer filtered by the project name
Microsoft Purview Audit log search for the code name
Content explorer filtered by sensitivity label
An eDiscovery keyword search, then an export

explanation: eDiscovery searches mailboxes, Teams, OneDrive and SharePoint using keyword queries and conditions, and the results can be exported for delivery to counsel. Activity explorer reports on activities involving labeled content, not message content by keyword. Audit log search finds records of user and admin actions, not the messages themselves. Content explorer shows items by label or sensitive information type rather than by arbitrary keywords for legal production.

prompt: A legal team has collected 200,000 documents for a case and wants to reduce the time reviewers spend by grouping textually similar documents and identifying the emails that give the complete context of each thread. Which two premium eDiscovery capabilities help? (Choose two.)
explanation: Premium eDiscovery analytics on review sets include near duplicate detection, which groups textually similar documents, and email threading, which identifies the messages that give the complete context of a conversation, so reviewers can review a fraction of the documents. Content markings are sensitivity label headers, footers and watermarks. Search and delete removes harmful messages rather than organizing review. Adaptive scopes target retention policies at users or sites by attribute.

prompt: Many of the documents collected for a case are scanned images of signed contracts. Investigators need the text inside those images to be searchable after the content is added to a review set. Which eDiscovery capability provides this?
explanation: When content is added to a review set, eDiscovery OCR extracts text from images and includes it with the content so the image text can be searched. Conversation threading collects whole Teams and Viva Engage conversations. Advanced indexing reprocesses partially indexed items but does not read text from images. Decryption opens content protected with Microsoft encryption technologies.

prompt: A phishing email that slipped past filtering has been delivered to hundreds of mailboxes. The compliance team wants to find every copy and remove it from users' mailboxes using Microsoft Purview. Which capability should it use?

options.text: An eDiscovery hold on all mailboxes
A retention policy with a one-day deletion period

explanation: eDiscovery includes search and delete, which finds email messages, Teams chat messages and other content across the organization and removes potentially harmful items. A hold would preserve the phishing email rather than remove it. A retention policy that deletes content after one day would affect all mail, not just the phishing message, and is not a targeted cleanup tool. Audit intelligent insights show who accessed mail but do not delete it.

prompt: An important document disappeared from a SharePoint site three weeks ago. The site owner wants to know which user deleted it and exactly when. Which Microsoft Purview solution should be used?
explanation: Microsoft Purview Audit captures user and admin operations, such as file deletions in SharePoint, in the unified audit log, and the audit search tool can find them by activity, user and date range. Content explorer shows items that currently exist with labels or sensitive information. Compliance Manager tracks regulatory controls. Insider Risk Management analytics evaluates potential risk across the organization rather than answering who performed a specific action.

prompt: A company with Audit (Standard) learns that an incident began eight months ago, but its audit search only returns records from roughly the last six months. Microsoft Purview should keep Exchange, SharePoint and Microsoft Entra audit records for a year by default. What does it need?

options.text: An eDiscovery hold on the audit log

explanation: Audit (Standard) retains audit records for 180 days, while Audit (Premium) retains Microsoft Entra ID, Exchange, OneDrive and SharePoint records for one year by default and supports audit log retention policies for longer periods. SharePoint storage quota does not affect audit retention. A Sentinel workbook can only display data that has been ingested and does not change Purview audit retention. eDiscovery holds preserve content, not audit records.

prompt: After an attacker compromised a mailbox, investigators need to determine precisely which email messages the attacker accessed, including the sensitivity labels of those items, to scope the breach. Which capability provides this level of detail?

options.text: The default 180-day audit retention in Audit (Standard)
Activity explorer's 30-day view of label changes
Audit (Premium) intelligent insights, such as the MailItemsAccessed event
A Defender for Cloud regulatory compliance report

explanation: Audit (Premium) intelligent insights include events such as MailItemsAccessed, with properties like the sensitivity label of accessed mail items, which help investigators determine the scope of a compromise; users need an Audit (Premium) license for these events to be logged. Audit (Standard) retention defines how long records are kept but does not add these insights. Activity explorer focuses on activity involving labeled content, such as label changes, not per-item mailbox access. Defender for Cloud compliance reports assess cloud resource configuration.

prompt: A regulated firm must keep audit records of certain executives' activities for ten years. It already has Audit (Premium). What else is required?

options.text: A 10-Year Audit Log Retention add-on license for those users and an audit log retention policy
Nothing, because Audit (Premium) retains all records for ten years by default
Exporting audit records to CSV every 180 days
A records management label on each executive's mailbox

explanation: Retaining audit records for ten years requires a 10-Year Audit Log Retention add-on license assigned to the users plus an audit log retention policy covering them, and it is not retroactive. Audit (Premium) by default retains Exchange, SharePoint, OneDrive and Microsoft Entra records for one year, not ten. Manual CSV exports are a workaround rather than the supported retention capability. Records management labels apply to content items, not audit records.
